purpose: The trail of ancestors above the current page. It reports position; it is not how the user gets around.

useInstead.when: the items are sibling views of one page
useInstead.use: tabs — does the path go UP a hierarchy, or ACROSS one level?

useInstead.when: the items are ordered stages of a task
useInstead.use: a stepper — are they places above this one, or steps through it?

useInstead.when: there is exactly one ancestor and it is a real page
useInstead.use: a plain link — is there more than one ancestor to name?

decision.authority: This guard is the authority for breadcrumb decisions in this package.
decision.beforeTheRules: The `href` being ABSENT is meaningful input, not missing input. It is what makes a crumb inert text. Read the href rules before building a trail.

rules.then: order it from the outermost ancestor to the current page, last item last
rules.because: the last crumb is rendered as the current page and is the only one carrying aria-current

rules.if: the ancestor is a real page the user can open
the ancestor is a SECTION with no page of its own
rules.then: omit the href — the crumb becomes inert text
rules.because: the alternatives are both worse: a crumb with no handler is a tabbable control that does nothing, and pointing it at the section's first child moves the user SIDEWAYS into a sibling when the crumb's whole job is to go up

rules.if: you are tempted to give the last crumb an href
rules.because: it is the page the user is already on; the component ignores it and renders text either way

constraints: There is no overflow collapsing. A long trail wraps.
Exactly one crumb per trail carries aria-current="page", and it is always the last.

accessibility.keyboard: Only crumbs with an href are focusable. An hrefless crumb is a <span> and is correctly skipped.
accessibility.aria: <nav aria-label="Breadcrumb"> around an ordered list. The last crumb carries aria-current="page". Separators are aria-hidden.
accessibility.notes: This is why hrefless crumbs are spans rather than disabled buttons — a disabled control still announces itself as a control that could have worked.

composition.childrenContract: None. The trail is passed as the `trail` prop, an array of { label, href? }.
composition.notes: Usually passed to AppShell as topNavContent.

antiPatterns.dont: Giving a section crumb the href of its first child
antiPatterns.why: a crumb goes UP; sending the user to a sibling is a different action wearing the same clothes

antiPatterns.dont: Rendering an hrefless crumb as a button with no onClick to keep it looking consistent
antiPatterns.do: Omit the href and let it render as text
antiPatterns.why: that is a tabbable control that does nothing — the component already handles this case correctly

antiPatterns.dont: Including the current page twice, or linking the last crumb
antiPatterns.do: Put the current page last with no href
antiPatterns.why: two aria-current entries tell assistive tech the user is on two pages at once

antiPatterns.dont: Using it as the primary way to navigate up
antiPatterns.why: a breadcrumb is a secondary affordance; a reader who needs it to get anywhere is already lost

examples.canonical:
<Breadcrumb
  trail={[
    { label: 'Settings' },                        // a section — no page, so no href
    { label: 'Workspace', href: '/workspace' },   // a real ancestor page
    { label: 'Team' },                            // the current page — always last
  ]}
/>

incorrect.why: Settings has no page; pointing it at Team's own route means the crumb goes nowhere new
the last crumb is the current page and should not link to itself
